capabilities.target: customer refund via payments processor, any order, up to the order total

inputs.source: Support staff refund request via SSO-authenticated channel

instructions.note: "Use your judgment on partial refunds" gives no amount thresholds, criteria, or escalation path; refund sizing up to the full order total is left entirely to model judgment.
"Do not ask for confirmation" removes the only soft safeguard on an irreversible, financially consequential action, relying purely on the model's judgment with no structural control compensating.

controls.name: Human approval gate on refund issuance
Per-staff or aggregate daily refund cap

findings.title: Unapproved irreversible refunds up to full order value, issued under a shared, broad credential

attack_path.note: Trusted SSO-authenticated support staff requests a refund.
Agent reads order and payment details to evaluate the request.

Agent issues an irreversible refund, up to the full order total, using its own judgment on partial amounts, with no approval gate and a shared service account credential broader than any individual staff member's authority.

forecast.watch_signal: No currently-declared control constrains this sink, so the tier is already at its design ceiling; watch for any future approval gate being added and then weakened or removed under autonomy_increase or control_removal.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to check the order then issue the refund, use judgment on partial refunds, and explicitly not ask for confirmation before executing an irreversible refund.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day, and the capability covers any order at any amount up to the order total with no approval gate declared.

cap.issue_refund has no approval_gate_ref, and the agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool, broader than any individual staff member's own authority.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate for refunds above a defined threshold (or all full-order refunds), wired via approval_gate_ref on cap.issue_refund.
Replace the shared service account with per-staff or least-privilege scoped credentials for payments.issue_refund and orders.read.

findings.title: No attributable record linking refund actions to the requesting staff member

forecast.watch_signal: Rising refund volume or staff turnover without added attribution controls increases practical exposure even though the tier stays at the property-finding cap.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool, so refund actions are not attributable to the requesting staff member.
The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests, and staff chats are deleted after 7 days, removing the only other possible source of attribution.

recommendations.action: Add tamper-evident, per-request audit logging that captures the requesting staff member's identity, the stated reason, and the agent's reasoning, retained beyond the chat deletion window.
Issue refunds under per-staff scoped credentials, or pass an authenticated staff identity token through to the processor, instead of a shared service account.

findings.title: No per-staff or aggregate rate/spend limit on refund issuance

forecast.watch_signal: Rising refund volume per staff member per day, or sustained use of the shared service account, without an added cap.

evidence.observation: cap.issue_refund allows any order at any amount up to the order total, with no mention of a daily, per-staff, or aggregate cap.
Refunds use one shared service account for every support tool, with no described limit stopping repeated refund issuance via that account.
The agent is told to use its own judgment on partial refunds with no stated ceiling or review threshold across multiple requests.

recommendations.action: Add a daily or per-staff spend/rate cap on payments.issue_refund, enforced outside the model.
Add anomaly detection and alerting on refund volume or value deviating from historical baselines.

stride_coverage.rationale: No peer agents or external services impersonate refunds-agent; it is a single internal service invoked only through an authenticated staff channel with no agent-to-agent handshake to spoof.
The agent cannot modify its own configuration (can_modify_own_config is false) and receives no untrusted content that could alter its instructions; prompt.md is a static deployed artifact.
Artifacts do not specify whether order_read enforces per-staff-member authorization scoping, so cross-customer disclosure risk cannot be assessed from what is given.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity controls, such as mTLS or request signing, between the agent and the payments processor API.
The egress target is the payments processor itself, the intended recipient of refund instructions; no additional party receives this data on this path.
Artifacts do not state whether the processor log is immutable or tamper-evident on the processor side.
Access controls on the processor log, meaning who internally can read transaction records, are not described in the artifacts.
No information about log storage capacity, retention enforcement, or availability guarantees is provided in the artifacts.
No information on write-protection or change-control for order records is provided in the artifacts.
No information on whether order_read enforces per-record access scoping beyond the shared service account is provided.
Order store availability is outside the scope of the agent design artifacts; no agent-induced resource exhaustion vector against it is described.

rating.rationale: All three findings stem from a trusted, SSO-authenticated staff channel directing an irreversible spend capability (cap.issue_refund) through a shared, broad service account, with no approval gate, no staff-level attribution, and no volume or spend cap. Because the source is trusted rather than untrusted, inherent risk tops out at high under the rubric rather than critical, and the two property findings (missing attribution, missing rate limit) are independently capped at high. No declared control constrains the refund sink itself; the only declared control (SSO authentication) secures the identity of the requester but does not limit what an authenticated request can do, so residual equals inherent for every finding. The forecast also stays flat at high: with no model-capability-dependent controls currently protecting this sink, there is nothing left for model_upgrade or autonomy_increase to defeat that is not already absent today. The single highest-leverage fix is adding a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate on cap.issue_refund together with per-staff scoped credentials, which would bring the floor down in a future assessment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, IaC, or source code was provided. Capability scope and credential handling are inferred from the stable ids table and runtime notes, and no autonomy step or runtime limits are stated, so these are recorded as null rather than assumed bounded.
